narrative: At 2,251 m, drag increased sharply before the string stuck firm against the Gas-Bearing Sand while picking up after a survey. Mud overbalance against the depleted interval was estimated at 40 bar, and the string could not be moved even with 80 tonnes of overpull. A back-off was required; the free point was found and the lower assembly fished over 2 days. Recommend reducing mud weight toward the minimum safe window and minimising stationary time across depleted sands.

Stuck pipe occurred at 2,116 m while making a connection after a fast drilling run through soft Bokabil Shale. Cuttings returns had thinned out over the previous stands while ROP averaged 35 m/hr, pointing to poor hole cleaning and cuttings accumulation in the Bokabil Shale. Back-reaming and circulating for 7 hours cleared the pack-off and the string came free. Recommend frequent short trips and high-viscosity sweeps when penetration rates exceed 35 m/hr in reactive clay.

The drill string became stuck at 2,235 m while pulling out of hole through the Bokabil Shale section. The stuck point was shallow in the open hole where a directional survey recorded 4.5 deg/30 m, indicating a keyseat groove rather than differential sticking. The string was freed by working pipe and reaming through the keyseat over 4 days. Recommend limiting tripping speed through build sections and reviewing BHA stiffness in high-dogleg wells.

Partial losses began at 2,066 m in the Fractured Limestone and progressed to total losses within 2 hours. Flowline returns ceased completely with a pit loss of 7 cubic metres, consistent with a natural fracture network in the Fractured Limestone. A high-viscosity LCM slug regained partial returns and a cement squeeze sealed the zone after 1 days of remediation. Recommend monitoring pit volume closely and holding a dedicated LCM inventory when drilling the fractured carbonate in this field.

While drilling the shallow Alluvial Gravel Beds, losses reached 3 cubic metres per hour at 475 m. The shallow sequence took fluid at 3 cubic metres per hour without any change in drilling parameters. Two LCM pills of walnut shells and calcium carbonate reduced losses, followed by a soft cement squeeze; drilling resumed after 32 hours. Recommend maintaining adequate kill margin and expecting losses of several cubic metres per hour in the boulder beds.

A gas kick was detected at 3,335 m in a thin sand within the Barail Sandstone after a 34-minute connection stoppage. The flow check showed a 1.3 cubic metre pit gain and shut-in casing pressure of 105 bar, indicating a live kick. The well was shut in and killed using the wait-and-weight method within 9 hours. Recommend increasing mud weight margin and monitoring flowback closely below 3,335 m in this field.

While drilling the Carbonaceous Shale section at 2,283 m, torque climbed progressively from 15 to 26 kilonewton-metres and the hole began to pack off on each connection. Repeated pack-off events and rising drag indicated a swelling Carbonaceous Shale, confirmed by 14-inch caliper enlargement over the open hole. Stabilisation took 6 days of reaming and a mud programme change to an inhibitive KCl-polymer system at 1.23 SG. Recommend drilling the Carbonaceous Shale in one bit run with an inhibitive mud and avoiding long static periods.

While drilling the Carbonaceous Shale at 3,198 m, H2S detectors alarmed at 28 ppm near the shale shaker. Operations were paused, breathing apparatus donned, and scavenger added to the mud as a precaution. The zone was controlled within 4 hours and drilling resumed with continuous scavenger treatment. Recommend full H2S personal monitoring and breathing apparatus rigged up before coring below 3,198 m in this area.

Pump pressure dropped suddenly from 191 to 154 bar while drilling Tipam Sandstone at 1,807 m, indicating a washout in the drill string. A washout was confirmed at a worn tool joint; the string was pulled and the damaged joint replaced after 29 hours. Fishing recovered the full assembly and drilling resumed following a pressure test of the string. Recommend regular drill-collar inspection and tracking standpipe pressure trends to catch gradual washouts before a twist-off.

A shallow water flow developed at 372 m in the Shallow Aquifer Sand with a small pit gain of 0.6 cubic metres. The well was shut in and flow-checked, and mud weight was raised from 1.08 to 1.11 SG to overbalance the shallow aquifer, with the diverter rigged up as a precaution. Flow stopped after 8 hours and operations resumed with full returns. Recommend anticipating shallow water flow zones from seismic analysis before drilling surface hole in this block.

The pipe became differentially stuck at 3,304 m when circulation was stopped for a connection across the Gas-Bearing Sand. With 1.27 SG mud in the hole, the pressure overbalance against the depleted sand was close to 37 bar and no downward movement was possible. The string was freed after 4 days of spotting-fluid soaks and repeated jarring, with no pipe left in hole. Recommend reducing mud weight toward the minimum safe window and minimising stationary time across depleted sands.
